title: Fast and slow pointers
summary: Detect a cycle in a linked list in O(1) space. Slow moves one node, fast moves two; inside a cycle fast gains a node per step, so they meet. The Node class is shown, not typed.
code: # A meeting means a cycle exists.
while fast is not None and fast.next is not None:
triggers: cycle, middle or kth-from-end of a linked list in O(1) space
a sequence where next = f(current) might loop forever
prompts: Each kiosk in a museum points visitors to the next kiosk. Starting at the entrance, could someone who follows the signs walk in circles forever?
Each short link redirects to another link. Using constant memory, decide whether following redirects from one link ever loops.
invariant: Once both pointers are inside a cycle, the gap between them shrinks by one node per step.
mantra: Slow one, fast two; meeting means a loop.
pitfalls: Check fast and fast.next before reading fast.next.next.
Compare nodes with 'is': equal values are not the same node.
Cycle start: after they meet, restart one pointer at head and move both one step at a time.

anchors.name: Linked List Cycle II
anchors.trick: After meeting, reset one pointer to head; they meet again at the cycle start.

anchors.name: Middle of the Linked List
anchors.trick: When fast runs out, slow is at the middle.

anchors.name: Happy Number
anchors.trick: The list is n -> sum of squared digits; detect the loop the same way.

mutations.explanation: Fast no longer gains on slow: both land on the second node together, so every list of two or more nodes looks cyclic.
On a list with an odd number of nodes fast.next is None, so fast.next.next crashes.
